intended_object: The ideal (det(X) − 1) in the polynomial ring K[X_ij : i,j ∈ n] over a commutative ring K. It is the defining ideal of SL_n, so K[X_ij]/(det − 1) is the coordinate ring of SL_n. Inferred from the docstring, the name, and the next declaration, `PolynomialCoordinateRing`.
explanation:
`PolynomialRing K n` is `MvPolynomial (n × n) K`. `determinant K n` is the determinant of the generic matrix `Matrix.mvPolynomialX n n K`. So the definition is the principal ideal generated by det(X_ij) − 1, which is exactly the standard defining ideal of SL_n.

The setting is already general: any commutative ring K and any finite index type with decidable equality. The determinant needs both `Fintype` and `DecidableEq` on the index type. The only restriction is that `n` must live in the same universe as `K`, which comes from the shared `variable` line. This has no mathematical effect.

The file uses the ideal to give the polynomial presentation K[X]/(det − 1) of the SL_n coordinate ring, which it compares with the localized quotient. That use matches the intended object. I know of no Mathlib declaration that defines this ideal.
